data.howToHeading: How to brew moka pot coffee
data.tableNote: A moka pot cup is a small 2 oz serving, about 60 ml. The basket and the boiler set the ratio for you: fill the basket level and the water to just below the valve.

description: Moka pot coffee starts at a 1:10 ratio: 15 g of coffee to 150 g of water for a 3-cup pot. Scale it to any pot size, with the table and the stove method.

faqs.answer: Fill the basket level: about 15 g for a 3-cup pot, 30 g for a 6-cup pot. That works out to roughly 1:10 coffee to water. Do not tamp the grounds down.
faqs.question: How much coffee goes in a moka pot?

faqs.answer: Fill the boiler to just below the safety valve: about 150 g for a 3-cup pot, 300 g for a 6-cup pot. Never cover the valve.
faqs.question: How much water do I put in a moka pot?

faqs.answer: Usually the grounds cooked while the pot heated up. Start with pre-boiled water in the boiler, use medium heat, and take the pot off as soon as it gurgles.
faqs.question: Why does my moka pot coffee taste bitter?

faqs.answer: No. Level the basket with a finger and leave it loose. Tamping blocks the water, the pot sputters, and the coffee over-extracts.
faqs.question: Should I tamp moka pot coffee?

faqs.answer: About 150 ml of strong coffee, which is one small mug or two little 2 oz cups. A moka pot cup is 2 oz, not an 8 oz mug.

felicityNote: The moka pot is my weekend brewer. Pre-boiled water in the bottom, basket filled level, off the heat at the first gurgle. No shortcuts on any of the three.

parts.meaning: The ground coffee in grams, weighed before brewing.
The grams of water for each gram of coffee at the 1:10 starting ratio.
The water in grams. One millilitre of water weighs one gram, so grams and ml are the same number.

howToSteps.name: Fill the boiler
howToSteps.text: Boil the kettle first, then fill the boiler with hot water up to just below the safety valve. For a 3-cup pot that is about 150 g.

howToSteps.name: Fill the basket level
howToSteps.text: Spoon fine-ground coffee into the basket until it is level, about 15 g for a 3-cup pot. Do not tamp it down.

howToSteps.name: Assemble and heat
howToSteps.text: Screw the top on firmly and put the pot on medium heat with the lid closed. The coffee should start flowing in three to four minutes.

howToSteps.name: Take it off at the gurgle
howToSteps.text: When the stream turns pale and the pot gurgles, take it off the heat at once. Stir the coffee in the top chamber and serve straight away.

lede: Moka pot coffee starts at 1:10, one gram of coffee for every 10 grams of water. A 3-cup pot takes 15 g of coffee and 150 g of water, and the pot itself sets the ratio.

table.caption: Moka pot coffee to water by pot size

title: Moka Pot Coffee to Water Ratio
tutorial: The moka pot is the one brewer where the ratio is mostly decided for you. The basket holds a set amount of coffee and the boiler holds a set amount of water, and together they work out to roughly 1:10. A 3-cup pot takes 15 g of coffee and 150 g of water.

Published ratios run from 1:7 to 1:12, which looks like disagreement until you remember the pot sets the dose. Fill the basket level without tamping it down, and fill the water to just below the safety valve, and you land near 1:10 whatever the pot size. That is the starting point this calculator uses.

A moka pot cup is small: about 2 oz, or 60 ml. A 3-cup pot makes about 150 ml of strong coffee, which is one small mug or two little cups. If you want a full mug, brew the pot and top it up with hot water, or make it the base of a milk drink.

Start with pre-boiled water in the boiler. Cold water sits on the heat longer while the pot comes up to pressure, and the grounds cook in the meantime, which tastes bitter. Boiled water means the coffee brews in four to five minutes and the pot comes off the heat as soon as it gurgles.

Grind fine, like table salt, but never tamp the basket down. Tamping blocks the water and the pot can sputter or stall. Level the grounds off with a finger, screw the top on firmly, and use medium heat. When the coffee gurgles and the stream turns pale, take it off the heat.
